relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own header (Pacific Journal of Mathematics vol. 154 no. 1, 1992, the period matrix of Bring's curve, two authors) and matches the seeded key exactly, including volume, issue and year. Three citation sites, load-bearing, and the CONTENT checks out — but the LOCATOR does not. Both QOU/Archimedean/BringHauptmodulGate.lean:39 and QOU/BraidKnot/TrBIntegerTracePrune.lean:53 attribute their claim to 'Thm 1', and they attribute TWO DIFFERENT statements to it: the first says 'Thm 1: residual gauge Gamma_0(5) on Bring's modulus', the second says 'Thm 1: the stabilizer acts on H_1(Bring, Z) by integer symplectic matrices (entries 0, +-1)'. In the scanned text the Gamma_0(5) statement is LEMMA 1 (p. 184): a symplectic M commuting with the automorphism representation has a specific block form, and 'if in addition M is integral then m, n, p and q are integers and 5 divides p, i.e. M in SpGamma_0(5)'; the immediately following result establishes that SpGamma_0(5) is contained in the stabiliser of Bring's half-plane. The integral homology action the second site needs is developed in §2 (the induced matrix [f]_* on H_1(B,Z) in a canonical basis built from the 20-sided hyperbolic polygon), and the phrase 'entries 0, +-1' does not occur in the text. Caveat on my own check: the PDF is a poor-quality scan and its OCR mangles headings, so I can state that no 'Theorem 1' heading is recoverable from the extracted text and that Lemma 1 carries the Gamma_0(5) content, but not that a Theorem 1 provably does not exist. Third site QOU/Archimedean/BringEllipticFactor.lean:57 cites it alongside two other sources for the elliptic-quotient structure; the document does construct the elliptic quotients (E_1 = B/<(2345)> shown to be an elliptic curve with modulus mu, and a second E_2 = B/<(24)(35),(25)(34)>), so that use is supported.

keyResults.statement: An integral symplectic matrix commuting with the S_5-automorphism representation on H_1 lies in SpGamma_0(5) (the block form forces 5 | p), and SpGamma_0(5) is contained in the stabiliser of Bring's half-plane.
keyResults.useForFolio: It is the residual-gauge input BringHauptmodulGate leans on for the discrete t_5 = -10 pass/fail gate. Same content the corpus already uses — only the locator needs correcting from 'Thm 1' to 'Lemma 1'.

keyResults.statement: Construction of a canonical homology basis for Bring's curve from a 20-sided non-euclidean polygon with angles pi/5, pi/4, pi/2, and the explicit integral matrices by which the automorphisms act on H_1(B, Z).
keyResults.useForFolio: This, not a 'Theorem 1', is where the integer homology action cited by TrBIntegerTracePrune actually lives.
